description_en: Gajendramokṣa Nārāyaṇa Mandirais, located in the small courtyard of Ṭuṃbāhāl Ṭol, houses a stone statue of a six-armed Gajendramokṣa Nārāyaṇa sitting cross-legged on a Garuḍa. He is holding a wheel, an arrow and a conch in his right hands and a club, bow and lotus in his left hands. According to a KVPT report (KVPT2000, 4), the original statue was stolen in 1980 CE and a new statue was enshrined in 2013 CE. The three-tiered, west-facing temple stands on two plinths with a colonnade, supported by 12 columns. The temple features a gilt pinnacle crowning its apex, along with a smaller pinnacle positioned on the middle roof, facing west.The temple is encompassed by an oil lamp balustrade. Positioned in front of the temple is a bell, supported by a stone stand. Towards the northwest, there is a well, while to the southwest, one can discover a smallcaityaand adharmadhātu maṇḍala.The inscription on the southern wall of the temple attributes its construction to Luṁgu Bhāro in 1576 CE (NS 696), mentioning his endowment ofguthiland for sustaining daily worship. Unfortunately, theguthiis currently inactive, and the whereabouts of its land are untraceable. Responding to the plea of local residents, Ghanashyam Sharma of Tilā Ṭol has taken on the responsibility of performing the daily ritual worship of Gajendramokṣa Nārāyaṇa.Prior to the reconstruction by the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust in 2000 CE, the temple had suffered extensive damage. The roofs of the top two tiers were completely lost and the lowest roof had partly collapsed. The restoration effort integrated four of the original struts, while all other struts were carved anew (KVPT 2000: 53). Unfortunately, the 2015 CE earthquakes again caused significant damage, requiring the temporary stabilization by means of wooden bracing. 6 years later, in 2021 CE, through the initiative of KVPT, all ground-level walls were reconstructedin situ, and the roof structure underwent repairs.
description_ne: पगोडा शैलीमा बनेको तीन छाना भएको र पश्चिम तर्फ फर्किएको गजेन्द्रमोक्ष नारायण मन्दिर टुंबाहाल टोलको सानो चोकमा रहेको छ, जुन चोक वल्खु टोलबाट स्वथ जाने बाटामा पर्छ । यो मन्दिर दुईवटा पेटीमाथि बनेको छ । मन्दिरको भुइँतलाको चारै दिशामा काष्ठस्तम्भहरू छन् । मन्दिरको शिरको गजुरबाहेक दोस्रो छानामाथि पनि एउटा गजुर रहेको छ । मन्दिरको पेटीमा उक्लिनका लागि चार वटा खुड्किला छन् र कुँदिएको ढोकाभित्रको मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा गजेन्द्रमोक्ष नारायणको शिलाको मूर्ति छ । छवटा हात भएका नारायण गरुडमाथि पद्मासनमा बसेका छन् । उनका दायाँ हातहरूमा चक्र, वाण र शङ्ख छन् भने बायाँ हातहरूमा गदा, धनु र पद्म छन् । यो मन्दिरसँग सम्बन्धित केभिपिटि प्रतिवेदन (KVPT 2000: 4) मा यो मन्दिरको पुरानो प्रतिमा सन् १९८० मा चोरी भएको कुराको जानकारी दिइएको छ । सन् २०१३ मा नयाँ प्रतिमा प्रतिस्थापना गरिएको थियो ।यो मन्दिरको वरिपरि दीपमालिका राखिएको छ, अनि मन्दिरको अगाडि ढुङ्गाको बिममा झुण्ड्याएर एउटा घण्टा राखिएको छ । मन्दिर प्राङ्गणमा उत्तरपश्चिम कुनामा इनार छ भने दक्षिणपश्चिमपट्टि एउटा सानो चैत्य र एउटा धर्मधातु छ ।मन्दिरको दक्षिणी गाह्रोमा टाँसिएको शिलालेखमा यो मन्दिर नेसं ६९६ मा लुंग भारोद्वारा बनाइएको कुराको जानकारी दिइएको छ ।  त्यस शिलालेखमा मन्दिरको नित्य पूजाको लागि गुठी राखिएको कुराको पनि जानकारी दिइएको छ, तर अहिले गुठी जग्गाको अत्तोपत्तो छैन । स्थानीय जनताको अनुरोधमा तिला टोल बस्ने घनश्याम शर्माले मन्दिरमा दैनिक पूजाआजा गर्दैआएका छन् ।
brick_type: stone, mā apā (regular fired brick), dāci apā (conical veneer brick)
monument_assessment: Restored, Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number LAL1720_I_001 Sources Stone stele inscription embedded in the temple's south wall. H: 48 cm, W: 28 cm This inscription is published by Vajrācārya VS 2056, 34-37.

historical_events.event_description: In 1576 CE (NS 696), Luṃgu Bhāro built this temple in memory of his late grandson Deva Bhāro. Luṃgu Bhāro first visited Kashi (Varanasi) and established a statue of Umāmaheśvara on the wall of the Siddheśvarī temple there. After returning from Kashi, he built Gajendramokṣa Nārāyaṇa Mandira.
The Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust restored the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of the new Nārāyaṇa statue
historical_events.event_description: After the historic Nārāyaṇa statue was stolen in 1980 it took 33 years to initiate the commissioning of a new statue. The new statue was installed in accordance with tradition on Monday, November 2013.
After sustaining damage during the 2015 earthquakes, the temple underwent restoration once again, thanks to the efforts of the Kathmandu Valley Preservation Trust.
